Latur: The BJP-led Maha Yuti government led by Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis has made elaborate plans to make Maharashtra drought-free, veteran Marathwada politician and former minister Basavraj Patil said.

Patil, a veteran leader of the Lingayat community, described the current drought situation as serious; however, he said that the people will respond to the natural calamity with grit and determination.

“People have tremendous faith in Deva Bhau,” Patil, who is an MLC from the Dharashiv-Beed-Latur local authorities constituency and the BJP Latur Rural President, told DH.

“Taking into account the difficulties faced by farmers, the state government has announced various concessions and measures for drought-affected areas. These include a moratorium on recovery of crop loans, concessions on electricity bills for agricultural pumps, exemption from land revenue, educational concessions for students, and urgent arrangements for drinking water and fodder,” said the former Minister of State for Rural Development.

.‘Around 7% surface water left’: Patil warns of Maharashtra’s looming drought crisis.

Patil, who has extensive knowledge in the agriculture and cooperatives sector, said that the government is responding to the situation. “The water situation is going to be bad in the days to come. We have to conserve and judiciously use water. Supplying drinking water will be the priority,” he said, adding that people of Marathwada has seen drought in 1972 and the 1993 earthquake. “While this time the situation may be worse than the 1972-73 drought, the government is making all efforts to ensure that relief reaches the people,” he said.

Patil said the government has announced a series of relief measures for these regions. “Collectors of all drought-affected districts have been directed to complete crop damage assessments immediately. Authorities have also been asked to collect photographs and GPS coordinates to document the actual condition of crops and ensure transparency in the assessment process,” he said.

“Relief has also been announced on agricultural electricity bills. While electricity bills for agricultural pumps up to 7.5 horsepower had already been waived, pumps with higher capacity will also receive concessions,” he added.
